question: Why do nominally complete high-boundary paths near 10-12 km lose Monte Carlo completeness under the current independent per-bin signal-noise model?

model.signal_perturbation: independent Gaussian per native range bin using persisted one-sigma RCS uncertainty
model.path_survival_probability: product of single-bin positive probabilities along the contiguous backward path
model.caveat: This is an analytic diagnostic of the current independent-noise perturbation model, not a validated empirical vertical covariance model.

moderate_10km_probe.interpretation: The nominal path is robust per realization; the all-300-valid requirement can still fail occasionally because many very small tail risks accumulate.
No individual native bin has >1% non-positive risk, but aggregate path/ensemble risk is non-zero.

support_edge_probe.finding: Fragility is distributed across many weak native bins, mostly isolated or in short clusters rather than one extended missing layer.
Many weak isolated/short-cluster bins make complete backward support fragile even though the nominal path contains no missing/non-positive bin.

decision: Retain strict no-gap semantics. The observed failure pattern justifies testing declared pre-retrieval aggregation as a precision/resolution trade, not interpolation or gap filling.
relationship_to_followup: The subsequent 60/120 m aggregation experiment directly tests this weak-bin hypothesis and is frozen in 20251107sapm_vertical_aggregation_support_edge.json.
